advisor_identified: Historian of early modern Europe at the University of Victoria; supervisor of Axel Schoeber’s Gerard Roussel dissertation.

doctorate.title: Farcical Theatre and the Reformation of Manners in France, 1500-1650

evidence.says: UVic’s faculty biography states that Beam earned her History PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 1999 and began teaching at UVic in 2002. Its graduate-student list includes Axel Schoeber’s PhD, Gerard Roussel: An Irenic Religious Change Agent, matching the entry.

The department’s 2001–2002 newsletter introduces Sara Beam as new faculty, dates her Berkeley PhD to 1999, and names her doctoral thesis Farcical Theatre and the Reformation of Manners in France, 1500-1650.
The Paris Institute for Advanced Study identifies Beam as a University of Victoria historian and states that she received her MA and PhD in History from the University of California, Berkeley.

notes: The linked record matches her name, department, institution and exact thesis title. Its year is 2000, whereas both UVic sources date the PhD to 1999; the reason for this discrepancy was not established. The newsletter’s relevant passage was available in indexed text; its image PDF did not yield extractable text.
